found.title: Property Bridging Loans UK Guide: Purchase, Sale & Refurbishment Finance
found.summary: Blog/guide page with distinct 'Bridge to Purchase' and 'Bridge to Sale' sections. Bridge to Purchase: bridging is used to buy property quickly because it can be arranged in days or weeks rather than the months a traditional mortgage can take. Bridge to Sale: a loan secured on the property being sold lets the borrower access funds before the sale completes, then the sale proceeds repay the loan. This is the closest thing surfaced to a Bridge to Purchase / Bridge to Sell page body; no standalone product page for either was returned.
verbatim: Bridging loans are commonly used to purchase a property, due to their fast and flexible nature.
Bridging loans, on the other hand, can be arranged in a matter of days or weeks
A property bridging loan (secured against the property on sale) can enable the borrower to access funds quickly, without having to wait for the sale of the property.
Once the property eventually sells, the borrower can use the proceeds of sale to repay the bridging loan.
found.notes: Query 4. Snippet wording came back in the tool's summary as direct page text. Section heading on page is 'Bridge to Sale' (not 'Bridge to Sell').

found.title: Wealth Management (title as returned by search in this pass; sibling pass recorded 'Types of Borrowing - Silver Oak Capital')
found.summary: Overview page listing Bridge to Purchase and Bridge to Sell among its bridging finance types. States interest is paid as a lump sum at the end of the term, that bridging needs no affordability assessment, and gives a typical broker fee of 1.00% (1.50% for loans outside the UK).
verbatim: Bridging loans are quick to arrange and do not require any affordability assessment, with the loan interest paid as a lump sum at the end of the term
found.notes: Query 4. The '1.00% / 1.50% outside UK' fee figures were given in the tool summary, not as a quoted snippet. Page title returned as 'Wealth Management' in this pass, which looks like a page-section title rather than the real <title>.

found.title: Why Are Property Bridging Loans Popular in the UK?
found.summary: Blog page with a short 'Bridge to Sale' section noting that properties can sit on the market for months in a slow market, which is when a bridge to sale is useful.
verbatim: Properties can often spend months (or even years) on the market, especially in a slow market.

found.title: Property Finance FAQs
found.summary: FAQ page distinguishes Silver Oak's 'equity release' from retiree lifetime mortgages: what it offers is a short-term bridging facility, typically 12 to 24 months, which must be repaid within the term, whereas 'Equity Release' for retirees usually refers to a 'Lifetime Mortgage' with no repayments until death. Also says released funds can cover a tax bill provided there is a clear exit strategy, and that the firm helps clients with equity release for additional purchases or investment opportunities.
verbatim: The product we offer is a Bridging Loan.
found.notes: Query 5 and 6. The 12-24 month term and lifetime-mortgage contrast were given in the tool summary as paraphrase; only the one sentence is certain verbatim. This is the only equity-release explanation surfaced; no dedicated Equity Release page appeared.

found.title: HMO Finance UK
found.summary: HMO page carrying buy-to-let criteria: most BTL products max out at 75% LTV (25% deposit), with borrower profile and property type possibly requiring more; most lenders prefer 12 months' ownership of a standard buy-to-let before an HMO, but Silver Oak works with lenders who permit first-time landlords to buy HMOs given strong personal income and a clear management strategy. Also mentions equity release on HMO properties, lending against investment value rather than bricks-and-mortar value.

most lenders prefer you to have owned a standard buy-to-let for at least 12 months
